newsitem.title: UK: CWC likely to float 14.7 pct stake on Monday.
newsitem.headline: CWC likely to float 14.7 pct stake on Monday.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC), Britain's biggest and newest cable telephone and television group said on Friday it was likely to float a 14.7 percent stake in London and New York on Monday.

The flotation, which is not big enough to propel the new company into the FTSE, has been expected since CWC was formed in 1996 by merging the Mercury unit of Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc with the three British cable TV units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada.
CWC confirmed late on Friday that 97.9 percent of Bell Canada shareholders and 92.4 percent of NYNEX shareholders had approved the recommended offer.
"The management are pretty confident that dealing (in the new shares) will begin on Monday," a company spokeswoman told Reuters. She said only a few, minor details remained to be finalised.

CWC, which will be British Telecommunications Plc's biggest rival and has an estimated value of around 4.5 billion pounds ($7.3 billion), said it would release a statement on the London stock exchange on Monday confirming the start of trade.
Analysts expect trading to begin at 1330 GMT to coincide with the opening of the New York stock exchange.

With assets worth about 4.5 billion pounds, CWC will provide a broad range of local, national and international voice and data services and, in some regions, multichannel TV and internet computer services.
